speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
before: The barrier creaks up. The road to the D.N.A. is open.
after: The barrier creaks up, and the road to the D.N.A. is open.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
before: Halt. Passage through this checkpoint requires a permit, and no permit has ever been issued. Please take a number.
after: Halt. Passage through this checkpoint requires a permit, and I regret to inform you that no permit has ever been issued. You may take a number while you wait.

speaker: Prudence Pallor
before: APPROVED. ...That was the wrong stamp, and it felt... nice. Disregard that.
after: APPROVED. ...Oh. That was the wrong stamp, and I am afraid it felt rather nice. Please disregard that.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
before: Application denied; reapply in ten to twelve centuries. This is our express service.
after: Your application has been denied. You may reapply in ten to twelve centuries, which I am required to tell you is our express service.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
before: Not yet, then. You may take another number, though it will also be zero.
after: Not today, then. You are welcome to take another number and try again, though I should mention that it will also be zero.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: Oh! A customer! Hello. I'm Gerald, the breakroom barista, and also Number 4,000,212. They're on 3, so I brought a book. Well, several. All of them, actually.
after: Oh! A customer! Sorry, hello. I'm Gerald, the breakroom barista, and I'm also Number 4,000,212. They're on 3, so I brought a book. Well, several. All of them, actually.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: I make coffee for people who can't taste it, so nobody ever sends a cup back. Mind the machine in the corner, though: it's half miracle and half a different kind of miracle.
after: Most of my customers are ghosts and can't taste a thing, so nobody's ever sent a cup back, which is a great comfort to me. Do go gently with the machine in the corner, though. It's very old, and it sulks.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: Cream? None. Sugar? None. Hope? Out of stock, but we're expecting a shipment in 2090.
after: I'm so sorry, we're out of cream, and out of sugar, and if I'm honest we've been out of hope for a while as well. I did put in an order for more, and they say 2090, so I'm trying to be patient.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: They're still on 3. I wrote a memo about it, and the memo before that said 3 as well. I'm keeping them all in a folder, for when it changes.
after: They're still on 3. I checked this morning, and then I checked again in case I'd been rude about it the first time. I write it down in a folder every day, so that I'll know the minute it changes.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Welcome to the Department of Necrotic Affairs, dear. I'm Agnes Overdue, front desk. I died at this desk forty years ago and I've been employee of the month ever since. Nobody else qualified.
after: Welcome to the Department of Necrotic Affairs, dear. I'm Agnes Overdue, and I look after the front desk. I died at this desk forty years ago, and I've been employee of the month ever since, because nobody else applied.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Here's your number, dear: 4,000,213. We're serving 3. Ten years ago {villain}'s people filed some paperwork, and they filed it properly, and now the whole Department works for him.
after: Here's your number, dear: 4,000,213. We're serving 3, I'm sorry to say. Ten years ago {villain}'s people filed some paperwork, and they filed it properly, and ever since then the whole Department has worked for him.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Back again, dear? You're the only one who ever leaves. Since the transfer, not one soul in this building has passed on, and that includes me.
after: Back again, dear? It does me good to see somebody come and go. Not one soul in this building has passed on since the transfer, you see, and I'm afraid that includes me.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: The Records Basement elevator wants Form 13-B, and nobody has one. I applied for one, dear, but the application form is a 13-B.
after: If you're wondering about the Records Basement elevator, it wants Form 13-B, and nobody has one. I did apply for one, dear, but it turns out the application form is a 13-B.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: I'd help you more, but I'd need a permit to help you, and I have it on good authority I won't get one.
after: I'd do more for you if I could, dear, truly I would. I'd need a permit to help you, though, and I have it on good authority that I shan't be getting one.

speaker: Clerk Ledgerbone
before: Requisitions. I'm Clerk Ledgerbone, junior clerk, third class. Cards are issued in triplicate, and every one is Necrocrat-issue: authorized, stamped and slightly haunted.
after: This is Requisitions, and I am Clerk Ledgerbone, junior clerk, third class. Cards are issued here in triplicate, and every one of them is Necrocrat-issue: authorized, stamped and slightly haunted.

speaker: Clerk Ledgerbone
before: The stamp is haunted. It asked the new management for a raise and was denied, and it has taken that very personally.
after: For the record, it is the stamp that is haunted, and not the cards. It applied to the new management for a raise, the application was denied, and it has taken the matter very personally ever since.

speaker: Clerk Ledgerbone
before: No returns and no exchanges. Exceptions require Form 13-B, which I gather you've heard about.
after: I must inform you that there are no returns and no exchanges. An exception may be requested on Form 13-B, which I gather you have already heard about.

speaker: Clerk Ledgerbone
before: Requisition something, or just stand near the desk. You make me look busy, and that's excellent work so far.
after: You are welcome to requisition something, or simply to stand near the desk. A visitor makes me look busy, which I have noted in your favour, and I would be obliged if you stayed a while.

speaker: Clerk Ledgerbone
before: Pass Director Ectomund's quiz and find one hidden stash in the filing mazes. The stashes are tucked in corners nobody visits, which here is all of them.
after: Two items remain outstanding: pass Director Ectomund's quiz, and find one hidden stash in the filing mazes. The stashes are kept in corners that nobody visits, which in this building describes most corners.

speaker: Clerk Ledgerbone
before: Audit closed. The auditors have gone home, which for them means back to their desks.
after: The audit is closed, and the auditors have gone home, which for them means going back to their desks. Your part in it is on file, and I have filed it somewhere I shall be able to find it again.

speaker: Clerk Ledgerbone
before: Compliance is auditing, and I need a fresh pair of hands for two things. One: pass Director Ectomund's re-certification quiz. Two: find a hidden stash in the filing mazes.
after: Compliance is conducting an audit, and I am required to supply a fresh pair of hands for two items. Item one is to pass Director Ectomund's re-certification quiz. Item two is to find a hidden stash in the filing mazes.

speaker: Clerk Ledgerbone
before: I cannot leave the desk. Policy. Also, my legs are on loan to Accounts. I await their return.
after: I would go myself, but policy forbids me to leave the desk, and in any case my legs are on loan to Accounts. I filed for their return some time ago, and I have not yet had a reply.

speaker: Clerk Ledgerbone
before: The quiz is passed and a stash is found, so both boxes are ticked, in ink. Oh. Oh, that's lovely.
after: The quiz is passed and a stash is found, so both boxes may be ticked, and I shall tick them in ink. ...Oh. Oh, that is lovely. I had quite forgotten what it is like to finish something.

speaker: Clerk Ledgerbone
before: A commendation. Do not try to cash it. Accounts enjoys that more than you would.
after: Please accept this commendation on behalf of Requisitions. I would advise you not to try to cash it, as Accounts would enjoy the attempt a good deal more than you would.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Three roaming staff, dear, on any floor. Processed, mind, not promoted. I confused the two once, and now he's my supervisor.
after: It's three of the roaming staff, dear, and you'll find them wandering on any floor. Do see that they're processed and not promoted, won't you? I mixed the two up once, and he's been my supervisor ever since.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: The backlog's clear, dear, and it'll be full again by Thursday. Still, it's nice to have a moment, isn't it? I don't get many.
after: The backlog's clear, dear, and I expect it'll be full again by Thursday, but that's Thursday's business. It's nice to have a quiet moment at the desk. I don't get many of them.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Oh good, someone with a pulse. I have a backlog, dear, and this one walks: three staff went feral over a deadline from the new management, and now they wander the floors.
after: Oh, good, somebody with a pulse. I've a backlog to clear, dear, and I'm sorry to say this one walks about: three staff went feral over a deadline from the new management, and now they wander the floors.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Would you process three of them for me, by duel, on any floor? We're not allowed to raise a hand to colleagues, and you aren't one, dear. You never filled out the form.
after: Would you process three of them for me, dear? By duel, I mean, and any floor will do. We aren't allowed to raise a hand to a colleague, you see, and you aren't one, because you never filled out the form.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Three! That clears the backlog. I couldn't tell you how many forms that closes, dear; I stopped counting in 1987. Here's your bonus.
after: That's three, dear, and it clears the backlog. I couldn't tell you how many forms that closes, because I stopped counting in 1987, but it's a weight off this desk and I'm grateful. Here's your bonus.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: Punch in at the time clock by the front desk and pour a cup at the coffee machine here, in either order. HR isn't picky. HR is just watching.
after: Punch in at the time clock by the front desk, and pour a cup at the coffee machine here. You can do them in either order, if that helps. HR isn't fussy about which comes first; it only likes to watch.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: You're one of us now, officially. I wouldn't read the contract if I were you. I read it once, and I'm still in line.
after: You're officially one of us now, which I hope is all right. I wouldn't read the contract, though, if I were you. I read mine all the way through, once, and I've been in line ever since.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: You're new to the floor, aren't you? Then it's mandatory onboarding: punch in at the time clock by the front desk, and pour a cup from the breakroom machine.
after: You're new to the floor, aren't you? Then I'm ever so sorry, but there's mandatory onboarding. You punch in at the time clock by the front desk, and you pour yourself a cup from the breakroom machine, just here.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: Please don't skip it. HR is in the walls, and these days HR reports to him. I try not to lean on the walls; it feels like oversharing.
after: Please don't skip it, if you don't mind my asking. HR lives in the walls here, and these days HR reports to him, so I try not to lean on anything. It feels a bit like telling them things.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: Punched in, caffeinated and compliant! That's onboarding done, so here's your welcome kit.
after: Oh, you've punched in, and you've had your coffee, and nobody's been written up for anything! That's your onboarding done, so here's your welcome kit.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: The welcome is the main part of the kit, and I said it as warmly as I could. I've been practising it in the queue for years.
after: The welcome is really the main part of the kit, so: welcome. I hope that came out warmly. I've had years in the queue to practise it, and I've never had anybody to say it to until now.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Lovely building. Can't collect a single soul in it, mind. The paperwork won't let me past the lobby, and I've been sat here since the transfer.
after: Lovely building, this. Can't collect a single soul in it, mind, because the paperwork won't let me past the lobby, so I've been sat here with my flask ever since the transfer.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: I took a number, heh. Makes a change. Usually I'm the one calling them.
after: They gave me a number and all, same as everybody. Makes a nice change, that, seeing as I'm usually the one who calls them. Heh.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Appointments. Let's see, you're... hm. Not for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.
after: Appointments, same as ever. Now let's see, you're... hm. No, you're not down for a good long while yet. Lovely! That's what I like to see.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: A small silvery ghost is already in the queue, hugging an enormous stack of appeals tied with three kinds of ribbon. "Number 4,000,213. There you are, dear."
after: A small silvery ghost is already in the queue, hugging an enormous stack of appeals tied with three kinds of ribbon. "Number 4,000,213? There you are, dear. I've been keeping an eye out for you."

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: "I'm Agnes Overdue. I work the front desk, and on my lunch hour I'm an appellant: forty thousand appeals, every one denied. They've started decorating the stamps."
after: "I'm Agnes Overdue. I work the front desk, and on my lunch hours I appeal against the transfer. That's forty thousand appeals, dear, and every one denied, though lately they've started decorating the stamps."

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: "Follow me; I know where the departments hide. And a word of advice: the authorization is valid. That's what makes it so terrible."
after: "Come along with me, dear, because I know where the departments hide. And don't let anybody tell you the paperwork is forged. The authorization is valid, and that's what makes it so terrible."

speaker: (narration)
before: A small silvery ghost waves from the queue, the ribboned stack of appeals under one arm. "Number 4,000,213. I saved your place, dear. Nobody noticed, but then nobody ever does."
after: A small silvery ghost waves from the queue, the ribboned stack of appeals under one arm. "Number 4,000,213. I saved your place, dear, though I don't suppose anybody would have taken it."

speaker: (narration)
before: "I spent my lunch hour on appeal forty thousand and one, and it came back denied with a very nice stamp. I'm starting to take it personally."
after: "I spent my lunch hour on appeal forty thousand and one, and it came back denied with a very nice stamp. I do try not to take it personally, but they've had a great many chances."

speaker: (narration)
before: "Follow me; I know where the departments hide. And a word of advice: the authorization is valid. That's what makes it so terrible."
after: "Come along with me, because I know where the departments hide. And do remember, whatever they tell you up there, that the authorization is valid. That's what makes it so terrible."

speaker: D.N.A. staff
before: You wait until your legs ache. You check the clock above the door: four minutes.
after: You wait until your legs ache, and when you look up at the clock above the door it tells you that four minutes have passed.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
before: "You may appeal," he says. "You will lose. But you may appeal."
after: "You may appeal," he says. "You will lose, but you may appeal, and I would not want you to leave here thinking otherwise."

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Two aisles over, Agnes is filling in a form with a very stubby pencil. "Form 27-C, third attempt. It needs a 27-B, which needs a 27-C."
after: Two aisles over, Agnes is filling in a form with a very stubby pencil. "This is Form 27-C, dear, and my third attempt at it. It needs a 27-B attached, and the 27-B needs a 27-C."

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: "They keep stamping it DENIED and writing Irregular in the margin. Don't mind me, dear. I've filed worse and kept the receipts."
after: "They keep stamping it DENIED and writing Irregular in the margin, but don't you mind me, dear. I've filed worse than this in my time, and I kept the receipts for all of it."

speaker: Undersecretary Vellum
before: "The authorization remains valid. It was submitted, reviewed, approved, notarized and filed. You may appeal in triplicate."
after: "The authorization remains valid, having been submitted, reviewed, approved, notarized and filed. You may appeal in triplicate, and the appeal will also be noted."

speaker: Undersecretary Vellum
before: "Mr. Grimsby has asked me to hold the Court until his schedule opens. I will hold it very, very well. Noted."
after: "Mr. Grimsby has asked me to hold the Court until his schedule opens, and I intend to hold it very well indeed. Noted."

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
before: Your appeal has been received, reviewed and denied. It was a very good appeal.
after: Your appeal has been received, reviewed and denied. For the record, it was a very good appeal.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
before: You hold ticket 4,000,213. The display says NOW SERVING: 3. The queue snakes through the lobby, up the stairs and out of a window.
after: You hold ticket 4,000,213, and the display says NOW SERVING: 3. The queue snakes through the lobby, up the stairs and out of a window.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
before: "Even you. Especially you."
after: "That includes visitors," he adds, and he looks you over as though deciding where the seal ought to go.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby
before: The CE-No has been removed from office. By policy, the vacancy passes to the senior-most applicant on file. One moment. I will look it up.
after: The CE-No has been removed from office, and by policy the vacancy passes to the senior-most applicant on file. If you will allow me one moment, I will look it up.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby
before: ...The senior-most applicant is a ghost. It is, for the record, you, Ms. Overdue.
after: ...The senior-most applicant on file is a ghost, with forty thousand appeals to her name and every one of them correctly submitted. For the record, Ms. Overdue, it is you.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby
before: The procedure is clear: the office passes to you. You cannot appeal it, Ms. Overdue. I would only have to deny it, and I find I do not want to.
after: The procedure is clear, Ms. Overdue, and the office passes to you. I must advise you not to appeal it, because I would be obliged to deny you, and I find that I do not want to deny you anything more.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: I'm head of the whole Department now, and I'm still on the front desk. They gave me a big office, dear, but nobody waits in a big office. They wait here.
after: I'm head of the whole Department now, dear, and you'll notice I'm still at the front desk. They did give me a big office, but nobody waits in a big office. They wait out here, so this is where I'll be.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Mortimer's in the Waiting Room as number 4,000,214, learning to wait. It's going about as well as you'd expect.
after: Mortimer's in the Waiting Room as number 4,000,214, learning to wait. He isn't very good at it yet, dear, but he is trying, and Gerald has been ever so kind to him.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: That unfiled form. I kept it in my drawer for ten years, just in case. I think I'll keep it there a little longer. Something tells me it won't be needed.
after: And that form I never filed, dear, the third one. I've kept it in my drawer for ten years, just in case, and I think I'll keep it there a little longer. Something tells me it won't be needed.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Prudence is my deputy. She's much nicer than she used to be, and so, I'm told, am I.
after: Prudence is my deputy now, dear, and she's taken to it beautifully. She's a good deal gentler than she used to be, and I'm told that the same is true of me.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: Oh, it's you! Gerald, barista, and as of this morning Number 4,000,212: CALLED. I didn't know what to do with my hands, so I made coffee.
after: Oh, it's you! It's Gerald, the barista, and as of this morning it's Number 4,000,212: CALLED. I'm sorry, I'm still a bit wobbly. I didn't know what to do with my hands, so I made coffee.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: Agnes switched the queue machines off and called every number herself, one by one. It took all night. She never sat down.
after: Agnes switched the queue machines off and called every number herself, one by one, and she thanked each of us for waiting. It took her all night, and she never once sat down.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: Have a cup. It's free. The machine is feeling generous, and so am I.
after: Please, have a cup. It's free. The machine is feeling generous today, and for once so am I.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: No cream and no sugar, I'm afraid. None at all. But hope's back in stock, and I'm trying not to use it all at once.
after: There's still no cream and no sugar, I'm afraid, and I am sorry about that. But hope's back in stock, and I'm trying not to use it all at once.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: My number's been called. I asked Hob for one more pot before I go, and I'm making it last.
after: My number's been called, you know, really and truly called. I asked Hob if I might make one more pot before I go, and he told me to take my time, so I'm making it last.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: Mortimer's Number 4,000,214 now, and you were 213, right between us. Don't mention it to him, though. He goes very quiet.
after: Mortimer's Number 4,000,214 now, and you were 4,000,213, so you'd have stood right between us. I wouldn't mention it to him, though, if that's all right. He goes very quiet when it comes up.

speaker: Clerk Ledgerbone
before: Clerk Ledgerbone, Requisitions. The stamp has stopped haunting the place now that it got its raise.
after: Clerk Ledgerbone, Requisitions. I am pleased to report that the stamp has stopped haunting the premises, now that it has been given its raise.

speaker: Clerk Ledgerbone
before: It doesn't know what to do with itself, and neither do I. Cards, in triplicate, as always.
after: It does not know what to do with itself, and I must admit that neither do I. In the meantime the cards are issued in triplicate, as they always have been.

speaker: Clerk Ledgerbone
before: Apparently I am allowed to be unbusy now. I keep reaching for the stamp to certify it.
after: I am informed that I am now allowed to be unbusy. I keep reaching for the stamp to certify it, and then remembering that nobody has asked me to.

speaker: Clerk Ledgerbone
before: I've been practising. I just stood here for a whole minute and filed nothing at all. It was exhilarating.
after: I have been practising, however. Just now I stood here for one whole minute and filed nothing at all, and I do not mind telling you that it was exhilarating.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
before: Prudence Pallor, Deputy Head of the Department. Yes, I stamped DENIED on everything. I was tired, the paperwork was valid, and I am sorry.
after: Prudence Pallor, Deputy Head of the Department. For ten years I stamped DENIED on everything, because the paperwork was valid and I was too tired to ask whether it was right. I am sorry for it.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
before: {villain} did not corrupt us, you know. He used our own rules. Now I stamp APPROVED on things that deserve it.
after: {villain} did not need to corrupt us, you know, because our own rules did the work for him. These days I read a thing properly first, and I stamp APPROVED on whatever deserves it.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
before: The stamp is lighter than I remembered. Do you have anything I can approve?
after: The stamp is a good deal lighter than I remembered. I don't suppose you have anything with you that I could approve?

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
before: You had 4,000,213, and you did not wait. I keep thinking about that.
after: You held 4,000,213, and you did not wait for it to be called. I find that I keep returning to that.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
before: I made others wait far longer than you, and every one of them was a person. It is worse, knowing that now.
after: I made others wait a great deal longer than you did, and every one of them was a person. I did not know that then, and it is considerably worse to know it now.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Intake's moving again! Agnes waved me straight through. First time in ten years nobody's asked me for Form 27-B, and my appointment book is filling up nicely.
after: Intake's moving again, and Agnes waved me straight through with a smile. First time in ten years nobody's asked me for Form 27-B, mind, and the appointment book's filling up nicely. Heh.
